title: Enrol your child in primary school
kw: enrol school primary school starting school school place junior infants admission matricular escola criança
short: Children usually start primary school at 5 and must be in education from 6 to 16. You apply to the school itself, and applications for a September start usually open the October before.
facts: Usually from 1 October, a year ahead
steps: Look up schools near you with the Department’s **Find a School** tool.
Read each school’s admissions notice. It is published at least a week before applications open and gives the dates, the number of places and when you will get a decision.
Apply to the school by its deadline. You can apply to more than one.
Accept the place by the date the school gives you.

cases.q: What kinds of school are there?
a: Denominational schools have a religious patron. Multi-denominational schools, such as Educate Together, have no religious instruction during the school day. Gaelscoileanna teach through Irish.

cases.q: The school has more applicants than places
a: Its admissions policy sets out how places are given. A school cannot refuse a child on grounds such as disability, race or family status.

cases.q: Will I be asked to pay?
a: State-funded schools do not charge enrolment fees. A school may ask for a voluntary contribution: it is optional.

cases.q: We arrive in the middle of the school year
a: Contact the schools near you directly and ask whether they have a place.
See the [Back to School allowance](#/s/back-to-school) and [childcare subsidies](#/s/childcare).

src: Citizens Information · Choosing a primary school

title: Get money off childcare (National Childcare Scheme)
kw: childcare subsidy creche national childcare scheme ncs chick preschool nursery minder creche subsídio
short: Every family can get €2.14 an hour off registered childcare, whatever their income. Families with income under €68,000 can get more, up to €5.10 an hour. The money goes straight to the provider.
who: Parents of children older than 24 weeks and younger than 15 who use a registered childcare provider.
steps: Apply at **ncs.gov.ie**. You can choose the universal subsidy or the income-assessed one, whichever is better for you.
When approved you get a code called a **CHICK**.
Give the CHICK, with your child’s name and date of birth, to your childcare provider.
The provider registers your child and takes the subsidy off your bill.

a: Income-assessed if your family’s income after deductions is under €68,000: the lower the income, the higher the rate, and the full rate applies at €34,000 or less. Otherwise take the universal €2.14.
Phone the Parent Support Centre on (01) 906 8530 for a postal application. It takes longer.

title: Apply for a student grant (SUSI)
kw: susi student grant college university fees maintenance grant third level bolsa estudante faculdade
short: SUSI is the main grant for full-time students. Depending on family income it pays towards living costs, fees, or both. You apply online and do not need your exam results or a course offer to start.
who: You have lived in Ireland, the EU, EEA, UK or Switzerland for 3 of the last 5 years, and meet the nationality rules.
Your family income is under the limit: for example €47,010 for the full maintenance grant, or €64,315 for a 50% fee grant, for a family with fewer than 4 children.
You are on an approved course.
need: Your PPS number, an email address and a phone number.
steps: If you are provisionally approved, SUSI sends you a personal list of documents.
Post photocopies, not originals, to SUSI, P.O. Box 869, Little Island, Cork.

a: The closing date for 2026/27 was Thursday 5 November 2026. Contact SUSI on 0818 888 777 or support@susi.ie to ask about a late application.

There is a separate [part-time fee scheme](https://www.citizensinformation.ie/en/education/third-level-education/fees-and-supports-for-third-level-education/part-time-fee-scheme-for-undergraduate-courses/) for some undergraduate courses.
